1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183:

value.full_target: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1 with Chevalley generators x,y,h, every nonzero v∈V with xv=0 and hv=λv, and every arbitrary admissible lattice M⊂V (a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all x^r/r!,y^r/r!), prove that V(K)=M⊗ℤK is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V(K). Here L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗ℤK acts by the induced lattice operators, including the Chevalley construction in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure assumption on K is made, and λ=0 and p=2 are included.
value.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, including λ=0 and p=2, over the given arbitrary field K.

value.text: H003 gives n>0 and I has n elements. We prove the two string formulas by induction. At m=0, h v=λv and xv=0 by H005. For the step temporarily assume L1: h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v, and, if m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v (with xy^0v=0 at m=0). From [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h in H004, h y^{m+1}v=y h y^m v-2y^{m+1}v=(λ-2m-2)y^{m+1}v, while x y^{m+1}v=y x y^m v+h y^m v=[m(λ-m+1)+λ-2m]y^m v=(m+1)(λ-m)y^m v. This also holds at m=0 using xv=0. Discharge L1; induction proves the asserted formulas for all nonnegative m.

For every i∈I, iteration of F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v. For i=0 this is v with empty product 1. For 1≤i≤λ each factor is a positive integer and hence nonzero in ℂ. H005 gives v≠0, so y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Their h-eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct in ℂ. To check independence, fix arbitrary c:I→ℂ and j∈I, and temporarily assume L2: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. Apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id). Every term except the j-th is zero; the remaining term is c_j∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. The product and e_j are nonzero, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary every coefficient is zero. Discharging L2 and quantifying over c proves that the whole family is linearly independent.

Apply M003 with A=ℂ, T=V, Q=I and f=e. F001 makes I finite and nonempty; F002 supplies independence; H004 and card(I)=n=λ+1 give the required dimension equality. Thus e spans V, so together with independence it is a basis. F001 at m=λ+1 says y^{λ+1}v, if nonzero, is an eigenvector of eigenvalue -λ-2. Expand this vector in the e-basis. Applying h-(-λ-2)Id shows each coefficient times (λ-2i+λ+2)=2(λ+1-i) is zero; these eigenvalue-difference factors are nonzero scalars for i∈I. Hence every coordinate is zero and y^{λ+1}v=0. All higher powers vanish by further application of y.

Divide the string identities F001 by i!: e_0=v, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, he_i=(λ-2i)e_i; directly ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, and ye_λ=0 by F003. For r≤i, iteration and division by r! give X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_{i-r}=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r}; if r>i the iteration passes xe_0=0. Similarly Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ, and otherwise is zero by F003. These binomial numbers are integers (they count r-element subsets of a set of the indicated nonnegative size). This proves the basis, termination and all the asserted action formulas.

By H006 choose an integer basis of M that is also a complex basis of V. Its index set is finite because V has finite complex dimension (H004). M002 applied to this complex basis over ℂ counts its elements as dim_ℂ V=n. N001 gives card(I)=n, so reindexing gives an integer basis indexed by I. This proves F001. H001 ensures R is a subring: products of integers not divisible by the prime p are again not divisible by p, and addition and multiplication of the stated fractions preserve the denominator condition.

Choose f as in F001. M001 with A=ℤ, B=R and T=M gives the R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Under ι_R these vectors go to f_i. If ∑ r_i f_i=0 with r_i∈R, complex independence of f gives every r_i=0. Hence ι_R is injective. Its image contains f and therefore spans V over ℂ. This also proves that M_R is free of rank n. From now on identify M_R with this image.

Admissibility H006 makes every X_r,Y_r preserve M; their complex linearity then preserves the R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=[x,y]=xy-yx does too by H004. These integral operators obey the Chevalley brackets on M and therefore induce the stated action after tensoring. For any 0≤t≤λ, H003 gives t<p; applying M006 with ℓ=p to this arbitrary t and H001 gives p coprime to t!, hence p does not divide t!. Thus 1/t!∈R and t! is a unit. In particular λ!, j!, (λ-j)! are units for j∈I. The integer identity binom(λ,j)j!(λ-j)!=λ! shows that binom(λ,j) is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ-j)!/λ!.

def R (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ := Subring.closure {q | ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
instance rModule (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def MR (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V := Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def DP {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V := (r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • f^r
def e {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := DP y i v

1: # Postprocessing: connect checked nodes into the source-facing Lean proof
2: 
3: Use one fresh **postprocessing author thread** after every required local proof
4: is checked. This is a serial stage per problem and consumes none of the N
5: parallel proof slots. The existing mapping author serves this role; its output
6: drives actual assembly. The **independent Audit B reviewer** is a subsequent
7: fresh thread. Assembly authoring, standalone compilation, kernel inspection
8: and semantic review have different completion states.
9: 
10: ## Entry and immutable inputs
11: 
12: Require all planned proof bodies, exact interface/plan/source bindings and the
13: accepted NL0/Audit A authority. A missing producer or failed local job keeps
14: assembly blocked, even if all its consumers passed conditionally. Revalidate
15: the existing authority; do not rerun unchanged Audit A.
16: 
17: The author receives this problem's actual proof bundle, frozen contract/plan,
18: original H/E/M/N/P/D inventory, source-output map and own saved assembly
19: feedback. It may read its own checked proof bodies. Other cases, developer
20: history and hidden reference proofs remain unavailable. Do not preload all
21: background notes; retain their node-local reference locations.
22: 
23: ## Connection rules
24: 
25: 1. **Close the implementation DAG.** Use the frozen topological order and exact
26:    parameter/binder order. Supply each internal input with its actual checked
27:    producer; preserve implicit and instance arguments. Source-facing N outputs
28:    must use their recorded T realizations. Never replace a missing producer by
29:    an assumption, placeholder, opaque proof or changed target.
30: 2. **Discharge retained M ports.** Supply a real Lean proof of each port in
31:    `library_terms`, preserving required H/E. Any proved result in the pinned
32:    Mathlib environment may be used; no matching source-M name, library signature
33:    copy or permission ledger is required. New interfaces should normally apply
34:    the library directly and omit unnecessary M ports. A declaration name alone
35:    cannot discharge an assumption.
36: 3. **Export the original interface.** Retain all original H/E, parameters and
37:    definitions; remove M as assumptions by supplying the library proofs. Do
38:    not change representations, domains or hypotheses to force a match. The
39:    generator inspects the conditional theorem's actual universe parameters.
40:    Those occurring in retained parameters/H/E/conclusion are inferred from
41:    that interface. Only implementation-only levels absent from the retained
42:    interface are instantiated at zero at this application site; the general
43:    library declarations stay intact. Elaborate the generated assembled root
44:    synchronously (`set_option Elab.async false in`) so proof-only universe
45:    parameters are included at declaration commit. This does not serialize
46:    separate proof workers. Compile the
47:    result; do not guess that implicit inference succeeded.
48: 4. **Build a standalone artifact.** `Proof.lean` contains definitions, actual
49:    local proofs, connected conditional root, checked library discharges and
50:    final `AuditBExport.P`. It is compiled before audit instrumentation is
51:    appended. `assembly.json` and `assembly-compiler.json` record that real
52:    complete-file outcome. A conditional fragment is not this gate.
53: 5. **Prepare actual audit evidence.** After standalone assembly passes, inspect
54:    actual E/P kernel signatures and root closure. Carry short author
55:    correspondence notes for every E and complete P; relevant definitions and
56:    hidden fields remain visible to the independent reviewer. Save `Audit.lean`, `compiler.json`, `inspection.json`,
57:    correspondence, source/proof hashes and the review packet. Inspection has no
58:    default wall-clock or heartbeat budget. An explicitly requested cutoff or
59:    actual execution failure is an incomplete inspection, not a mathematical
60:    rejection. Full endpoint fidelity and kernel trust checks still apply.
61: 
62: ## Repair and handoff
63: 
64: Use `check_draft` for actual feedback and keep the saved candidate. The result
65: identifies the candidate and failing layer; compiler errors precede long
66: printed types. `read_assembly_feedback` reads only this author's candidate,
67: generated Lean, full compiler output or mechanical records in bounded pages.
68: Follow pagination when a short excerpt is insufficient. Correct legitimate
69: mapping/library-application/connection errors without restarting proof authors.
70: Submitting the identical checked candidate reuses its exact hash-checked native
71: result; this does not create a semantic review or a new PASS.
72: 
73: An actual missing/changed interface or source premise returns to the affected
74: boundary. A generator/tool defect is execution engineering; report the concrete
75: diagnostic and preserve the draft if it is outside the author's allowed edits.
76: Do not report a source paper unavailable merely because a short log was cut,
77: or call an unlocated name-format rejection a mathematical gap. No routine
78: progress essay or periodic model continuation is required.
79: 
80: Hand off only after **standalone assembly and mechanical inspection pass**.
81: The independent reviewer then reads complete source/formal pairs and actual
82: evidence under [Audit B](audit-b.md). It receives no author's suggested verdict.
83: `ASSEMBLY-PASSED`, `AUDIT-B-MECHANICAL-PASSED` and a structurally accepted mapping

Use action endomorphisms of the complex sl2 module; the three Chevalley brackets and common invariant subspaces encode its representation and irreducibility. lam remains an integer; l=lam.toNat and Idx l=Fin(l+1), with H003 justifying the identification. M is a Z-submodule of V (equivalently an additive subgroup). R is the subring of Q generated by fractions with p-prime denominators; T005 proves it is exactly Z_(p). MR is its span inside V; T006 constructs the tensor identification, not an assumed embedding. Jc is initially a span, and T009 proves its exact coordinate-set meaning. All tensor spaces are scalar-first: VK=K tensor_Z M is the canonical flip of the source M tensor_Z K. FirstChange/ScalarData record checked natural maps, not assumptions. IntegralOps records restrictions whose existence is proved, and baseChange gives the tensor-induced action. All result structures are witness records and their existence is a step obligation.

P.explanation: All fields K of characteristic p and all complex action modules and arbitrary lattices are quantified as parameters with the six original hypotheses. The three bracket relations present sl2(C), and common x,y,h-invariant subspaces encode irreducibility; the highest weight vector and dimension are retained. A Z-submodule is exactly an additive subgroup, and its simultaneous integer/complex basis can be indexed by Fin(l+1) since dim V=l+1. Generator stability is equivalent to stability under the generated U_Z. With 0≤lam, l=lam.toNat equals lam, so the range and dimension are unchanged. Tensor flip identifies K tensor_Z M with M tensor_Z K in both directions, intertwining each induced operator. IntegralOps contains only restrictions agreeing on every lattice element; such restrictions are unique. The existential witness therefore states the actual induced action, not a selectable new action. Nontrivial is nonzeroness; bottom/top are zero/the whole space. Invariance under x,y,h is equivalent to invariance under their K-linear span L(K), also in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure or distinct reduced weights are imposed.
